answer: Rotating Epoch Admission Lottery: each identity must submit a request whose arrival time lands inside a narrow per-epoch window derived from a shared kernel schedule. Requests outside their assigned slot are discarded, so an attacker flooding N identities must hold and time N distinct submissions, paying compute and scheduling costs per identity without batching gains. A walnut-shaped arrival histogram flags clusters for audit, and any identity whose slot misses twice is moved to a slow island queue with reduced admission odds.
